terms.origin: Claude Code (Anthropic); used throughout ORCHESTRATION-DESIGN-2026-10.

terms.origin: Coined by us in ORCHESTRATION-DESIGN-2026-10.

terms.definition: A check a change must pass before merging: tests, lint, claim checks, and reviewers finding no open critical defect. Also the step that runs a store entry's own check.
terms.origin: General software practice; our gate workflow is described in HARNESS-BOTTLENECKS section 3.4.

terms.definition: A plain JavaScript workflow script that gathers agent results and sorts them into buckets for the Fable judge.
terms.origin: Coined by us in ORCHESTRATION-DESIGN-2026-10.

terms.origin: Coined by us in ORCHESTRATION-DESIGN-2026-10.

terms.definition: A saved JavaScript script run by the Workflow tool. It issues subagents in a set order with agent(prompt, {schema, model, effort}) and returns one structured result.
terms.origin: Claude Code workflow feature.

terms.definition: A per-run log of finished agent results that lets a stopped workflow resume from its run id; knownDead lists ids that returned null last time. Not the same as the knowledge store’s journal of event files.
terms.origin: Claude Code workflow feature; the knownDead use is ours.

terms.definition: A script rule that stops issuing agents when fresh null results suggest a usage limit, halting with HALT and not_started lists.
terms.origin: A general software engineering pattern, applied in ORCHESTRATION-DESIGN section 4.3.

terms.definition: A fixed piece of text placed before every subagent prompt, giving the repository, branch, settled facts and rules.
terms.origin: Coined by us in the orchestration design and clinic launcher.

terms.definition: Project instruction files an agent session reads first. FixFlow's is long, so every session pays to read it; AGENTS.md is the equivalent convention for other agent tools.
terms.origin: CLAUDE.md is a Claude Code feature; AGENTS.md is an agent-tool convention.

terms.definition: A typed shape for agent output. The additionalProperties:false setting forbids extra fields, and a description keyword attaches plain-language meaning to a property.
terms.origin: Outside standard (JSON Schema).

terms.definition: The forced tool call a schema-bearing subagent must make to return its answer. The tool layer validates it and asks for a retry if it does not match.
terms.origin: Claude Code Workflow feature.

terms.definition: Stage-1 agents return facts only, never comparisons, severities or verdicts. Judgement is left to the main session.
terms.origin: Coined by us in ORCHESTRATION-DESIGN-2026-10.

terms.definition: The Opus agent that reads the live repository in a deep-dive lane and returns ranked, evidenced findings. Analysts produce claims; skeptics check them.
terms.origin: Coined by us in ORCHESTRATION-DESIGN-2026-10.

terms.definition: A fresh-context Opus verifier given only a claim, its evidence and its failing condition, and asked to trace or refute it. The number of skeptics per gate is capped.
terms.origin: Coined by us in ORCHESTRATION-DESIGN-2026-10.

terms.definition: A fresh-context agent, usually Opus at high effort, whose job is to disprove a claim, fix or design. It treats the claim as wrong until code, tests or sources show otherwise.
terms.origin: Coined by us in the orchestration method and harness sweeps.

terms.definition: A Sonnet pass that confirms quoted text exists where claimed and has not moved or been fixed.
terms.origin: Coined by us in ORCHESTRATION-DESIGN-2026-10.

terms.definition: The four skeptic outcomes. Unverifiable means neither proven nor disproven, and it carries the test that would settle it.
terms.origin: Coined by us in ORCHESTRATION-DESIGN-2026-10.

terms.definition: A review result in a fixed machine-readable form that names the head commit the reviewer read. See also Output shapes and Verdicts.
terms.origin: Coined by us in the bottleneck compile.

terms.definition: The input or state under which a defect claim can be observed.
terms.origin: Coined by us in ORCHESTRATION-DESIGN-2026-10.

terms.definition: Claims that were neither verified nor refuted, kept together with the test that would settle each one.
terms.origin: Coined by us in ORCHESTRATION-DESIGN-2026-10.

terms.definition: Finding severity from most to least serious. In the testbed, late P1 fixes sometimes created new defects, and many P3 ids were carried without a status.
terms.origin: Common triage convention; the scheme is used in the G2 gate and clinic reviews.

terms.definition: A check limited to items a change touched, plus the files one import away.
terms.origin: Coined by us in ORCHESTRATION-DESIGN-2026-10.

terms.definition: A markdown file that names a helper agent with its own prompt, tools and pinned model, selected through agentType or subagent_type. We have 11 [M] fixflow-* agents.
terms.origin: Claude Code subagents feature.

terms.definition: Two project agents we built: a Haiku code locator, and a pull-request reviewer bound to a head commit that returns a verdict schema.
terms.origin: Built by us in this repository.

terms.definition: Claude Code's built-in file-finding agent. It inherits the model tier of the session that starts it.
terms.origin: Claude Code feature.

terms.definition: A folder of instructions an agent loads for a kind of task, starting with a SKILL.md whose description says when to use it. We have 13 [M] skill packages.
terms.origin: Claude Code feature; our conventions are in .claude/skills/README.md.

terms.definition: Frontmatter is the header block of an agent file; its skills field loads the named skill's full text when the agent starts.
terms.origin: Claude Code.

terms.definition: UPSTREAM.md records where a sourced skill package came from: repository, commit, paths, licence, date. SPDX is the standard short licence identifier, for example MIT.
terms.origin: UPSTREAM.md is ours (.claude/skills/README.md); SPDX is an outside standard.

terms.definition: A step only I may perform; agents stop there. Written as [owner] in plans and skills.
terms.origin: Coined by us in .claude/skills/README.md.

terms.term: Output shapes (MAP, RESEARCH, FINDINGS, VERDICT, COMMANDS, SCAN)
terms.definition: Fixed schemas agents return. FINDINGS is an analyst's ranked claims, VERDICT a skeptic's ruling, and SCAN reports committed secrets as fingerprints.
terms.origin: Coined by us in ORCHESTRATION-DESIGN-2026-10, section 5.2.

terms.definition: Claude Code tools. The web tools must be loaded through ToolSearch before an agent can use them.
terms.origin: Claude Code tools.

terms.definition: A session-specific temporary folder outside the repository where agents write logs and working files.
terms.origin: Claude Code session environment.

terms.term: Hook (PreCompact, SessionStart, PostCompact, PreToolUse, PostToolUse, Stop)
terms.definition: A script Claude Code runs automatically at an event, such as before compaction, at session start or on stop. It can add text, block, or alter a tool call.
terms.origin: Claude Code feature.

terms.definition: A PostToolUse hook route that replaces a tool's result before the model sees it.
terms.origin: Claude Code feature, as recorded in our runtime audit.

terms.definition: A block in the project's .claude/settings.json that lists commands the agent may not run.
terms.origin: Claude Code feature.

terms.definition: A Claude Code permission mode in which subagents run without asking for approval.
terms.origin: Claude Code feature.

terms.definition: SendMessage sends a message to a running session. A parked start is a session created now and released later by a message.
terms.origin: SendMessage is a Claude Code tool; parked start is ours (card CR-02).

terms.definition: get_usage reports a session's tokens used and compactions. /context shows what fills the window: skills, connectors, CLAUDE.md.
terms.origin: Claude Code desktop and command-line features.

terms.definition: Claude Code's non-interactive command-line mode: one process per prompt.
terms.origin: Claude Code feature.

terms.definition: The saved record of a Claude Code session, one JSON line per message or call, pruned after 30 days [S] by default. JSONL is the one-record-per-line format.
terms.origin: Claude Code feature; JSON Lines is a general format.

terms.definition: Model Context Protocol, a standard for plugging tools and data sources into Claude. A connector is a linked outside service whose tool definitions add to window size.
terms.origin: Open standard from Anthropic; used by Claude Code.

terms.definition: The unit of text a model reads or writes. Usage, cost and window size are all counted in tokens.
terms.origin: General language-model field.

terms.definition: Everything the model sees on one call: system prompt, tools, earlier messages and results. With our compaction setting the practical ceiling is near 367k tokens [M].
terms.origin: General language-model field.

terms.definition: The tokens the model read, summed over every call, including cache reads.
terms.origin: Measure defined in TOKEN-BOTTLENECK-2026-11.md.

terms.definition: Tokens re-read from the prompt cache on each call at a lower price. Summed over calls they show how much context is carried: 4,253M [M] in November.
terms.origin: Anthropic API prompt caching.

terms.definition: Tokens newly stored in the prompt cache, counted separately from cache reads.
terms.origin: Anthropic API prompt caching.

terms.definition: A feature that stores a repeated prompt start so later calls can read it cheaply.
terms.origin: Anthropic API feature.

terms.definition: Tokens the model writes, including thinking. In the token study, 45 % [M] of them were thinking.
terms.origin: General language-model field.

terms.definition: One request to the model, which re-reads the whole window. The message id is its unique id, used to count each call once.
terms.origin: Anthropic API.

terms.definition: The roughly 70,000 tokens [M] each agent re-reads before doing work: system prompt, tool and connector schemas (34k [M]), skills, CLAUDE.md.
terms.origin: Claude Code subagent behaviour; measured in card CR-11.

terms.definition: Descriptions of every tool and connector loaded into the window. Deferred schemas list tools by name only and load full text when needed, shrinking the prefix.
terms.origin: Claude Code and MCP features.

terms.definition: Claude Code replacing a long conversation with a summary, plus a verbatim tail, so the session can continue. We counted 48 [M] in main sessions in November.
terms.origin: Claude Code feature.

terms.definition: A Claude Code setting, 100000 to 1000000 tokens [S], naming the size that triggers automatic compaction. A setting of 400000 [S] compacts near 367k [M].
terms.origin: Claude Code setting (/autocompact).

terms.definition: A compaction that uses a summary precomputed while the session sat idle. Default on, with a threshold of 200k tokens [S].
terms.origin: Claude Code setting idleCompaction.

terms.definition: The summary left after compaction, re-read on every later call. It was 8 % [M] of context tokens in the study.
terms.origin: Claude Code feature.

terms.definition: The plan's cap on use within a rolling five-hour period [S]. When it is reached, all work stops. How cache reads count against it is not yet known.
terms.origin: Anthropic plan feature.

terms.definition: Claude Code’s own spend counter (not our harness’s). Its totals are a lower bound, covering about one third [E] of the work.
terms.origin: Claude Code’s cost-state file, as described in the token-spend README.

terms.definition: A change that could cut token use, ranked by size in the token report.
terms.origin: Coined by us in TOKEN-BOTTLENECK-2026-11.md.

terms.definition: How much of the tokens sit where an idea or lever could act, for example calls past 200k. It is neither a saving nor a ceiling.
terms.origin: Coined by us in the bottleneck compile and token report.

terms.definition: The small group of files, about 72 [E] paths, that holds half of the fetched tokens across sessions.
terms.origin: Coined by us in the caching findings.

terms.definition: A short repository file of state, decisions, ruled-out items and next action that a session reads to resume. The clinic task.md also held the status table and gate sections.
terms.origin: Convention in the FixFlow and clinic harnesses.

terms.definition: Only the root session edits shared documents.
terms.origin: Coined by us in the clinic orchestration page.

terms.definition: The written instruction given to a session or subagent.
terms.origin: Ordinary usage; the clinic orchestration page.

terms.definition: Fan-out is the number of children per parent; depth is the number of session levels below the root (here root, slice sessions, at most one child level).
terms.origin: General usage; the clinic orchestration page.

terms.definition: Labels REPORTED, OBSERVED, DOCUMENTED, INFERRED, PROPOSED, UNKNOWN and VERIFIED that state how a fact is known.
terms.origin: Coined by us in the clinic AGENTS.md.

terms.definition: ff-gates.sh runs backend, mobile or web checks in containers with a per-lane database. ff-slot.sh is the machine-wide lock. Since 13 November it has two pools: a light pool of 3 [S] slots for backend gate stacks, and a heavy pool of 2 [S] for Jest, Vitest, an emulator or a Gradle build, which takes its whole pool.

terms.definition: A machine-wide permit to run the clinic’s full check, so heavy checks wait their turn instead of colliding on this PC. terms.definition: The clinic's full check: ruff, format, mypy, Django’s own checks (the clinic is a Django web app), migrations, database probe, pytest. Container mode runs it in a Linux Docker container: 230 s [M] versus 367 s [M] on Windows.

terms.definition: pytest-xdist runs tests in parallel workers. The serial pass is a second run for tests that cannot run in parallel, such as race tests.
terms.origin: pytest-xdist is an open-source pytest plugin; the serial pass is our usage.

terms.definition: The lane or worker count where the lowest limit is reached. Beyond it, more lanes or workers add queues and tokens but no speed. In the testbed the check’s knee was between 6 and 12 workers [M], and about three lanes [M] were worth running.
terms.origin: Capacity-planning and queueing practice.

terms.definition: A heartbeat is a periodic signal naming what a long check is doing. A stall watchdog kills a silent check; the stall limit is 600 s [S]. The check writes waiting, running or stalled.
terms.origin: General systems practice; the limit is a testbed setting.

terms.definition: A Windows feature that kills a whole process tree when its owner dies.
terms.origin: Microsoft Windows.

terms.definition: A script that merges slices one at a time under a lock, runs the check on the merged result and applies the board diff. Designed in harness v2.
terms.origin: Coined by us in the bottleneck compile, section 3.4.

terms.definition: Planner picks the lane count before work starts. Scheduler starts and resumes sessions. Governor slows the lanes so the five-hour usage window lasts. All three are harness v2 designs.
terms.origin: Coined by us in the harness v2 design.

terms.definition: The list of files a slice declares it will write. The plan check uses it to avoid collisions between lanes. Not the same as a knowledge-store entry’s footprint.
terms.origin: Coined by us in the harness v2 plan check.

terms.definition: Reinforcing (R) and balancing (B) feedback loops. R1 fix spiral, R2 context growth, R3 library compounds, R4 pile-up. B1 check capacity, B2 serial gate, B3 limit stop, B4 staleness, B5 lanes at knee.

terms.definition: Model quantities (stocks, such as slices waiting) and the rates that move them between states (flows).
terms.origin: System dynamics.

terms.definition: Owner decision cards on the harness v2 page, each with a phase and a when-needed date.
terms.origin: Coined by us in the harness v2 design.

terms.definition: Re-running a recorded fix chain or review at a frozen commit, in a clone with no later refs and a hashed answer key, so the agent cannot see the fix.
terms.origin: Coined by us in the bottleneck compile, sections 4 and 9.3.

terms.definition: A script mode that writes down what it would refuse or flag but blocks nothing, so it can be validated before it gets power.
terms.origin: Coined by us in the bottleneck compile, section 9.3.

terms.definition: The record listing every review finding with severity and status. Testbed rows were prose thousands of characters long, so a table is proposed.
terms.origin: Testbed practice; proposed as mechanism 4 in the bottleneck compile.

terms.definition: A list of permitted forms (citation styles, tools) so legitimate items are not flagged or refused.
terms.origin: General security and configuration practice.

terms.definition: A cleanup script that removes finished sessions or worktrees. It runs as a dry run first, only reporting what it would remove.
terms.origin: Coined by us in the bottleneck compile, for bottleneck B15.

terms.definition: A first-use walk on an empty database with no synthetic data: first user, import, a transaction, and close of day.
terms.origin: Coined by us in the clinic testbed work.

terms.definition: A case that must be detected, proving the check can find something. Every check that reports nothing found needs one.
terms.origin: Scientific method (laboratory and statistical practice).

terms.definition: Deliberate adversarial testing of a mechanism to find how it fails; eight [M] red-team defects were still open.
terms.origin: Security field practice.

terms.definition: Removing one lock to prove the named test then fails. A race test runs two concurrent actions to prove a lock stops the conflict.
terms.origin: Used in the clinic gate; general concurrency testing.

terms.definition: My numbered decisions on the clinic board: 21, the root may start the next slices itself; 22, approve a parallel-test dependency; 23, use the machine and a Linux container; 24, wrap up the build.
terms.origin: My decision log of the clinic build.

terms.definition: Numbered clinic review findings. Letters name the slice or review family (GS, GT, GU, GV; faster-check FC and FS).
terms.origin: Coined by us on the clinic task.md board.

terms.definition: Findings moved out of the gates to be fixed during the pilot. T15, T16 and T17 are plan acceptance targets; T17 covers page latency and load.
terms.origin: My decision USER-24; clinic technical plan.

terms.definition: A script that creates fake test data. Real labels without the SYN marker are refused by design.
terms.origin: Coined by us in the clinic build.

terms.definition: A local Debian virtual machine sized like the proposed server, running fifteen [M] re-runnable drills: deploy, upgrade, backup, restore, load and security probe.
terms.origin: Microsoft Hyper-V; the rig and drills are from the clinic staging-rig task.

terms.definition: Locust is an open-source load tester. N+1 is a page issuing many small database queries. fsync=off is a Postgres setting that skips disk flushes, safe only for disposable test databases.
terms.origin: Outside open-source projects and database practice.

terms.definition: A Windows socket state, and the 'No buffer space available' error seen on loopback connections.
terms.origin: Windows networking.

terms.definition: The ceiling on speed-up when only part of the work can be removed: if a share X of the time is removed, the best speed-up is 1/(1-X).
terms.origin: Amdahl's law, from computer architecture.

terms.definition: An outside study of 16 [S] developers in early 2025 that found AI access raised task completion time by 19 percent [S].
terms.origin: METR, an outside research group.

terms.definition: Open-source tools for evaluating and tracing language-model runs.
terms.origin: Outside open-source projects.

terms.definition: Outside agent-engineering projects that the clinic audited alongside HumanLayer's work.
terms.origin: Outside projects.

terms.definition: A rule-of-thumb token estimate (characters divided by 4) that undercounts by about 25-35 percent [E] in this repository.
terms.origin: A common rule of thumb.

terms.definition: Agent-written memory notes that Claude Code loads at the start of each session (15 [M] files in the clinic root).
terms.origin: A Claude Code feature.

terms.term: Context system (snapshot/restore, read admission, recall, resident input)
terms.definition: The clinic's tool around compaction. Snapshot saves declared task state and restores it verbatim; read admission limits big file reads (over 30 KB [S]); recall searches transcripts by words; resident input is what sits in the window.
terms.origin: Coined by us in the clinic's tools/context_system.

terms.term: Corpus map (cmap), status model S1-S6, query levels L1-L3, frontier, dangling endpoint
terms.definition: A versioned map of the clinic's planning documents, with edges and line spans, built by cmap.py. Statuses: attested, codebook, overlay, reconstructed, candidate, derived. Frontier: unexpanded referents. Dangling endpoint: named but unspecified target.

terms.term: Reader / reducer / pre-registration / arm / gates G0-G5
terms.definition: Reader extracts; reducer re-fetches and checks quotes. Pre-registration fixes test, gates and budget in writing before running. An arm is one condition in a comparison. G0-G5 are research checkpoints.

terms.term: MemTree / LCM / Virtual Context / YesMem / Cairn / Headroom / squeez / context-mode / claude-mem / CCH
terms.definition: Outside memory, compression and context-capping tools the clinic survey audited. Each limits only part of what enters the window; we adopted none.

terms.definition: Open-source Python tool that builds a knowledge graph from a mixed corpus using tree-sitter. Its 71.5x [S] claim compares tokens per graph query with reading every raw file. Used as a comparator arm.
terms.origin: Outside project safishamsi/graphify; PyPI package graphifyy.

terms.term: Call graph / blast radius / touch list
terms.definition: A call graph maps which functions call which. Blast radius, or touch list, is the set of functions, callers, importers, co-changing files and tests a fix could affect, attached to a reviewer brief.
terms.origin: General software practice; the script is proposed in HARNESS-BOTTLENECKS section 6.

terms.definition: tree-sitter is a local code parser covering about 40 [S] languages. ast-grep searches code by syntax tree, built on it.
terms.origin: Outside open-source projects.

terms.definition: Tools that fail the build when code crosses forbidden module boundaries: dependency-cruiser for JavaScript, import-linter for Python.
terms.origin: Outside open-source tools.

terms.definition: A hand-written map of where each capability lives in each runtime of the FixFlow repository.
terms.origin: FixFlow repository docs (docs/CODE-MAP.md).

terms.definition: Prompting schemes where the model writes several partial answers, then branches, votes or merges them. Reported gains were on puzzles with a 2023 model; not yet re-tested on current models.
terms.origin: Outside research papers.

terms.definition: An outside benchmark of real GitHub issues for coding agents. We cite it for fix-selection methods: voting alone among candidate patches resolved 25.7 % [S].
terms.origin: Outside benchmark, cited from the papers in our bottleneck research.

terms.definition: Spatial: a thing's neighbourhood in code and work. Temporal: when a fact became true and when it was replaced. Both are ways to look things up.
terms.origin: Coined by us in HARNESS-BOTTLENECKS-2026-11, section 6, 2026-11.

terms.definition: How often two files change in the same commit, used as a hint that they belong together. In the graph test it reached precision 0.26 [M] in a list of ten.
terms.origin: Software-evolution research; measured in our graph test.

terms.definition: A ranking that scores a node higher when well-linked nodes point to it. The personalised version restarts from a seed file so scores favour its neighbourhood. Aider's repo-map uses it.
terms.origin: Google's web-search ranking algorithm; used in the Aider tool.

terms.definition: Recall: share of true items found. Precision: share of returned items that are true. recall@8k: share of reference items inside an 8,000-token [S] answer, the graph test's main score.
terms.origin: Information-retrieval field.

terms.definition: One link step in a graph; three hops reaches things three links away from the starting point.
terms.origin: Graph theory.

terms.definition: Hub: a file many others depend on. Metapath: a typed route through the graph, such as calls, client URL, route, handler, then table write.
terms.origin: General graph field.

terms.definition: A graph whose nodes and links each carry a kind and evidence (file and line). Symbol-level means nodes are functions, classes and components rather than whole files.
terms.origin: General graph-database and code-analysis field.

terms.definition: A graph where a model reads text and code and writes meaning into it. A TKG also records when each fact became true and was superseded. Our parser-built graph was neither.
terms.origin: General AI field; outside systems such as Graphiti and Zep implement it.

terms.term: Graphiti / Mem0 / Letta / Zep / Copilot Memory
terms.definition: Outside agent-memory products we studied for ideas (two clocks, retire rather than delete, re-check when used) and for their failure modes.
terms.origin: Outside companies and open-source projects, studied in the knowledge-store research.

terms.term: GraphRAG / HippoRAG / RepoGraph / LocAgent / Aider repo-map
terms.definition: Outside systems that use graphs to help models retrieve or locate code, cited as prior art with mixed results. Aider's repo-map is a tree-sitter outline ranked by personalised PageRank.
terms.origin: Outside research papers and the Aider tool, as cited in our graph-test research.

terms.definition: LadybugDB 0.22.3 [S] is an embedded graph database, a maintained fork of Kuzu, whose upstream was archived in 2025. It was one graph-engine arm of the test.
terms.origin: Open-source projects; archive status as read in our graph-test research.

terms.definition: DuckDB is an embedded analytical SQL database; DuckPGQ is its extension that adds property-graph queries.
terms.origin: DuckDB project and a community extension.

terms.definition: A widely used graph database server (runs on the JVM). It was a candidate engine for the graph test but was not installed.
terms.origin: Neo4j, Inc.

terms.definition: SQLite is a small file-based database. FTS5 is its built-in full-text search with BM25 ranking. A recursive query follows links over several steps.
terms.origin: Open-source SQLite project.

terms.definition: The Linux Docker image, 1.26 GB [M], in which every graph-test arm runs so the arms share one environment.
terms.origin: Coined by us in the graph test engines-linux recipe, 2026-11.

terms.definition: The seed is the changed file or symbol given as the query. The reference is the other files and definitions the same commit changed.
terms.origin: Coined by us in graph2/protocol.md, 2026-11.

terms.term: T1 / T1x / T2 / T3 / T4 / T5 / TQ
terms.definition: Graph-test task sets: T1 change completion; T1x its cross-runtime subset; T2 changed code to tests; T3 documented chains; T4 defect register; T5 document lookups; TQ code-reading questions.
terms.origin: Coined by us in graph2/protocol.md, 2026-11.

terms.definition: Hypotheses declared before scoring: H1 and H2 engines equal; H1b community prior; H3 typed graph against baselines; H4 questions; H5 engine speed and size.
terms.origin: Coined by us in graph2 protocol addendum 3, 2026-11.

terms.definition: The 65 [S] June commits used to choose settings (tune) and the 75 [S] July-August commits scored once for the verdict (held-out).
terms.origin: General machine-learning practice; split defined in graph2/protocol.md.

terms.definition: A cheap baseline (same directory, plain co-change, or scripted search) that any graph method must beat to count as a gain.
terms.origin: Coined by us in the graph test protocol addendum 2, 2026-11.

terms.definition: The search baseline run as a fixed script. No agent decided what to search, and no agent was run in the held-out test.
terms.origin: Wording fixed by us in graph2 protocol addendum 6, 2026-11.

terms.definition: A stored grouping of related nodes, found by Louvain community detection, added to the ranking as a prior.
terms.origin: General graph-algorithm field.

terms.definition: A 95 % [S] interval from 10,000 [S] resamples by commit, and a permutation test for paired differences between arms.
terms.origin: General statistics.

terms.definition: Rank-quality scores: mean reciprocal rank, normalised discounted cumulative gain at ten, and area under the recall-against-tokens curve.
terms.origin: Information-retrieval field.

terms.definition: Running a model many times with each unknown drawn from its range, to see the spread of outcomes and which unknowns matter most, instead of one answer.
terms.origin: General statistics; I proposed it for the library pathway map.

terms.definition: A statistic showing how steadily one number rises or falls as another rises across runs; used to rank which unknowns move a result most.
terms.origin: General statistics, named for Charles Spearman.

terms.definition: Bounds on a rate from few trials: zero failures in n trials puts the true rate under about 3/n, so 0 in 40 gives 7.5 % [S]. Clopper-Pearson gives the exact one-sided bound.
terms.origin: Statistics field.

terms.term: P@1 / recall at shown / acted false positive
terms.definition: P@1: precision of the top result. Recall at shown: how many true entries appear in what is displayed. Acted false positive: a wrong lead someone acted on.
terms.origin: Information-retrieval metrics; applied in the knowledge-store design.

terms.definition: A calibration that removes one lookup key from an entry and checks the entry can still be found.
terms.origin: Information-retrieval evaluation style; named in knowledge-store research lane T-03.

terms.definition: A planned local database and command-line tool where agents record solved hard problems, traps and failed approaches and later look them up by symptom. Designed in PR #183, not built or proven.
terms.origin: Coined by us in KNOWLEDGE-STORE-DESIGN-2026-11.md, 2026-11.

terms.definition: The journal is an append-only folder of immutable event files in git, the source of truth. The index is a disposable SQLite database rebuilt from it for fast lookups.
terms.origin: Event-sourcing pattern; chosen as proposal D in the knowledge-store design.

terms.definition: Entry: one stored lesson. Handle: a key it is found by (error template, symbol, paraphrase). Footprint: the files, settings and versions it depends on, used to notice staleness.
terms.origin: Coined by us; footprint adapted from build-system dependency tracking.

terms.definition: Lookup outcomes: a lead is a confident, gate-checked match; a candidate is a weaker one; a miss is nothing found. Abstention means answering nothing when unsure.
terms.origin: Coined by us in the knowledge-store design, 2026-11.

terms.definition: Planned retrieval thresholds: lead at 0.5 [S], candidate at 0.3 [S], margin 0.2 [S]. They decide lead, candidate or miss and are to be frozen at KS-4.
terms.origin: Coined by us (decision D8) in KNOWLEDGE-STORE-DESIGN-2026-11.md.

terms.term: Trace / early cutoff / control pair / inject-control
terms.definition: Trace: fingerprint of the footprint at the last passing check. Early cutoff: keep an entry if its check still passes after a dependency changed. Control pair: two commits where the check must read present, then absent. Inject-control re-applies the failing pattern.
terms.origin: Trace and early cutoff from Build Systems a la Carte (ICFP 2018); controls coined by us.

terms.term: Probe / mutant / probe-in-lookup / valid_when / tri-state verdict
terms.definition: A probe is a small automatic check that a root cause is present; a mutant is a harmless edit it must ignore. valid_when is a precondition. Verdicts: applies, not_applies, inconclusive.
terms.origin: Coined by us; mutant idea from mutation testing in software testing.

terms.term: Entry kinds (do_not_apply, open_defect, trap, unverified_seed, pending_anchor)
terms.definition: A forbidden change, an unfixed defect, a gotcha, an entry awaiting its executable check, and an entry whose fix sits on a branch, in that order.
terms.origin: Coined by us in the knowledge-store design, 2026-11.

terms.term: Write gate / diff lookup / false-fire ceiling / caller-pin test / second door
terms.definition: Write gate: checks on recording. Diff lookup (ks lookup --diff): warns when a PR touches protected code. False-fire ceiling: one commit in ten [T]. Caller-pin test: fixes allowed callers. Second door: a path that skips a guard.
terms.origin: Coined by us (KS-2, D8, D17; my critique, 2026-11-03).

terms.definition: The knowledge store's planned build phases, one session each: audit, journal core, retrieval, gate, seed, pilot, Docker gates, wire-in, second host, checkpoint. KS-6b is the executable gate; KS-T is teardown.
terms.origin: Coined by us in the knowledge-store design, 2026-11.

terms.definition: Id prefixes in the design: rulings (R), adjudication (A), refuted claims (C), refuter amendments (F), critic amendments (K), my critique O1..O20, refuter pass P1..P27, second-pass claims (V).
terms.origin: Coined by us in sections 12.1-12.8 of the knowledge-store design, 2026-11.

terms.definition: My numbered decisions in the knowledge-store design, each with a default: KS-D1 run the recurrence audit, KS-D1b the build go-ahead, KS-D16 the embedding trigger, KS-D17 the CI caller-pin test, KS-D22 guarded_refs. The design writes them D1 to D22; this compile adds KS- so they never mix with the harness decisions D01 to D23.
terms.origin: Coined by us in the knowledge-store design, 2026-11.

terms.definition: Eight real past defects reconstructed from git history as first entries and test cases: ex6 correct-PIN lock, ex3 payment duplicate, ex4 dispatcher cursor, ex7 and ex8 Expo build traps.
terms.origin: Coined by us in knowledge-store research lane R-02, 2026-11.

terms.definition: BM25 is a word-matching formula whose scores only order results within one query. IDF weights rare words. IDF-weighted coverage is the share of a query's rare-word weight an entry matches.
terms.origin: Information-retrieval field; BM25 is built into SQLite FTS5.

terms.definition: Node's built-in SQLite module (release candidate) and the settings that let many readers and one writer share a file safely and wait briefly when it is busy.
terms.origin: Node.js and SQLite.

terms.term: Stampede / single-flight / claim / fencing token / Lamport counter
terms.definition: Stampede: several sessions repeating costly work. Claim: the first proceeds. Fencing token (claim_seq): marks a stale holder. Lamport counter: orders events from several writers.
terms.origin: Caching practice; Martin Kleppmann (fencing); Leslie Lamport (logical clocks).

terms.definition: A file named by the sha256 of its own sorted-key JSON bytes, so replaying an event is harmless. SHA-256 is the fingerprint used to pin versions.
terms.origin: General content-addressing practice.

terms.term: Memoization / case-based reasoning / KEDB / KCS / elastic-recheck
terms.definition: Memoization: reusing earlier answers. Case-based reasoning: solving by retrieving similar past cases. KEDB: known-error database. KCS: knowledge-centred service. elastic-recheck: OpenStack's tool matching failures to known-bug queries.
terms.origin: Computer science; Aamodt and Plaza 1994; ITIL practice; OpenStack.

terms.definition: ReasoningBank stores distilled lessons from agent failures and cut SWE-bench steps by 4-9 % [S]. Gloaguen et al. found repository context files raise cost over 20 % [S] without general success gains.
terms.origin: Outside research papers, cited in the knowledge-store design.

terms.definition: RRF: reciprocal rank fusion of rankings. doc2query: paraphrases generated and added at write time. sqlite-vec: a vector extension for SQLite. bge-small: a small local embedding model.
terms.origin: Information-retrieval research and open-source projects.

terms.definition: Facebook's learned method for choosing which tests to run for a change, cited as outside evidence for selective checking.
terms.origin: Machalica et al., ICSE-SEIP 2019.

terms.definition: Data leaving the machine to an outside service, here the model provider.
terms.origin: General security term.

terms.definition: A proposed separate memory of verified solutions that a cheap model fetches, adapts and reuses instead of calling a stronger model. Designed and modelled in the pathway map; not built or proven.
terms.origin: Coined by me; described in the harness v2 design and library pathway documents, 2026-11.

terms.definition: The order a failed problem climbs: one cheap retry, then Opus, then Fable, with the solution stored on the way back.
terms.origin: Coined by me in the library goal, 2026-11.

terms.definition: The library model's cost unit: one call by the cheap model (Sonnet) costs 1 [I]; other costs are multiples of it.
terms.origin: Coined by us in library-pathways model-brief.md, 2026-11.

terms.definition: My five expectations: E1 big token cut over time; E2 faster responses and builds; E3 Sonnet at low effort matching Opus; E4 reuse across projects; E5 accurate, efficient lookups.
terms.origin: Mine, stated on 12 November 2026.

terms.definition: A model of the library as a graph of states work passes through, with chances and costs on each branch. It shows the mechanism; its figures are model outputs from guessed inputs [G], not a forecast.

terms.definition: One saved, named change to the code in git. Reviews bind to a specific commit, and a finding closes on a commit.

terms.definition: A proposal on GitHub to merge a branch into main, with its changes, discussion and checks. Several of our design documents live as numbered PRs.

terms.definition: The last commit on a branch at the moment it merges. We want a reader to have read exactly this commit, not an earlier one.

terms.definition: One concrete defect or gap a reviewer or scan reports, with a path:line citation and a severity. It closes only on a test the harness runs.

terms.definition: One pass in which a reviewer reads a branch and returns findings, followed by fixes. The harness aims to cap rounds at two [T].

terms.definition: A reviewer returning a slice to its author with findings to fix, instead of passing it to merge. Each send-back adds a review round.
terms.origin: Testbed review loop; the fix-round contract limits how many are allowed.

terms.definition: A pass that fixes findings. The contract: a test per finding that fails before and passes after, full gate before the fix commit, revert instead of patching, a fresh reviewer.
terms.origin: Bottleneck B01 mechanism 9; to be replayed on recorded chains before live use.

terms.definition: A reviewer or agent started without the author's earlier conversation, so it cannot inherit the author's assumptions. Costs a new fixed prefix each time.
terms.origin: Refuter and fresh-reviewer practice; about 70k fixed tokens per agent [M].

terms.definition: The six labels we give every idea. Idea: written down, not yet designed. Designed: a written design exists. Built: the mechanism exists but has not been measured. Tested: measured or tried at least once. In use: part of how we work now. Parked: set aside for now, ruled out or replaced, and kept with the reason. A label is the furthest stage any source reports, which stops a design being described as a result.
terms.origin: This compile’s own honesty rule: a label never claims more than its sources report.

terms.definition: The check run directly on Windows rather than in a Linux container. Slower (6.1 minutes [M]) and hit by the loopback socket error; the container run is the faster route.
terms.origin: Bottleneck work on the gate; compare the container run at 3.8 minutes [M].

terms.definition: The most memory one check uses at its worst moment. It was never measured; the second check slot waits on it.
terms.origin: Bottleneck B07: slots are to be sized from one measured number.

terms.definition: A database private to one lane's checkout, with its own port and compose project, so parallel checks cannot corrupt each other.
terms.origin: Testbed isolation design; restarted by the restart chain.

terms.definition: A query of the knowledge store or library before exploring, triggered by an error, an escalation or a diff. It returns leads or abstains.
terms.origin: Knowledge-store design; lookup-only calls are what the index replay measures.

terms.definition: When a stored entry may no longer be true because the code changed. Handled by validity conditions and probes, not by time-based expiry.
terms.origin: Knowledge-store design; time expiry is on the do-not-build list.

terms.definition: The range expected to hold the true value in 95 of 100 repeats of a test. A difference smaller than the interval cannot be told from noise.
terms.origin: Statistics; used with the bootstrap in the held-out graph test.

terms.definition: A map of the code whose edges are labelled by kind (import, caller, test-of, crosses-runtime) rather than file-level imports only. Tried in the second graph test design.
terms.origin: My objections to the first graph test; replacement test protocol.

terms.definition: Software that stores nodes and edges and answers multi-hop queries natively, such as LadybugDB or DuckDB with graph support. Under test against SQLite.
terms.origin: Graph-test research; engine choice is my pending install decision.

terms.definition: A zero-token test: build an import-and-caller index at each recorded window's start, count the lookup-only calls it would have answered. First candidate trial of phase 3.
terms.origin: Harness v2 design, phase 3 and decision D23.

terms.definition: A generated view of slices, verdicts and findings, each with the commit it became true at and the commit that replaced it. Replaces the hand-edited board.
terms.origin: Harness v2 library first half; board target under 20 KB [T] from 221 KB [M].

terms.definition: A script that closes or reopens a gate round without a model: for each closed P1 citing a test, it runs the test at the fix's parent and counts failures.
terms.origin: Harness v2 script 2; checked by a replay on the record.

terms.definition: A script reading the sessions' own tool-call records to show who read the final head, whether the gate ran before each fix, and root edits per merge.
terms.origin: Harness v2 script 3; replayed over the 10 and 11 November merges.

terms.definition: A file each slice commits listing what it claims, so a script can check every cited test exists, ran, and fails when its guard is removed.
terms.origin: Bottleneck B12; over 20 recorded overstatements [M] motivate it.

terms.definition: A rule that an environment fact reported by an agent or stated by me is checked by one command before it becomes a harness rule.
terms.origin: Harness v2 mechanism 7, from five facts the bottleneck list got wrong.

terms.definition: A verified bundle of every branch, plus uncommitted work and transcripts, copied off the PC nightly. Protects against the unexpected power-offs and disk loss.

terms.origin: Bottleneck B05; harness v2 phase 1.

terms.origin: Bottleneck B19; harness v2 phase 4.

terms.origin: Bottlenecks B19 and B20; free steps come first.

terms.origin: Our library and graph-test work (idea MSR-18), kept by WP8.

terms.definition: A time when no FixFlow phase is running or waiting on its reviewer and no heavy check holds a slot on this PC, so a harness check or agent run cannot slow the ship lanes.
terms.origin: Our own term in this compile, from the harness v2 rule that the ship plan comes first.

terms.definition: The first-come order of FixFlow’s slot lock (ff-slot.sh): each waiting job drops a ticket and is served in arrival order. A light job may pass a heavier one only until the heavier one has waited 900 s [S], so neither kind can starve.
terms.origin: docs/program/lab/ff-slot.sh, added on 13 November 2026 after one lane waited 20 minutes [M] while later arrivals were served.

terms.definition: A Git Bash setting that stops it rewriting arguments that look like Unix paths into Windows paths. With it set, paths are written as C:/… .
terms.origin: MSYS2, the Unix layer under Git for Windows.

terms.definition: A git setting that lets Git for Windows create files whose full path is longer than Windows’ old limit of 260 characters. We pass it per command (git -c core.longpaths=true) when cloning into scratch folders.
terms.origin: Git for Windows.

terms.definition: One time the five-hour usage limit stopped agent work. October had 14 [M].
terms.origin: Our harness review and token measurement.

terms.definition: Replacing a file by writing the new version beside it and renaming it over the old one in a single step, so anything reading the file sees either the whole old version or the whole new one, never half of each.
terms.origin: Standard file-system practice; FixFlow’s gate scripts land changes this way so a running lane never reads a half-written script.

terms.definition: Every workflow is saved as a script before it runs, so it can be re-run and its result checked against the saved version.
terms.origin: Our orchestration design; adopted through WP10a.

terms.definition: A balanced search tree used by databases. Inner nodes hold only keys that route a search and all data sits in the leaves; a node that outgrows its size splits in two, and small neighbours merge.
terms.origin: Database systems, 1970s; in the database lectures on our list (MTH-67).

terms.term: Split and merge (of sessions) / split line
terms.definition: In my B+ tree proposal (PAR-22), sessions are nodes of a distributed system: leaves do the work, inner ones route and gate. One whose window passes the split line hands its work, by scope, to two fresh sessions (a hand-over), and two small siblings join into one. The line is a share of the window, set per model; about 40 % [S] is the outside rule of thumb, 400k [E] on our windows.
terms.origin: My proposal of 14 November 2026; the 40 % figure came with the Dex Horthy sweep and is untested here.

terms.definition: A model stating something that is not so: a report that overstates what was done, an invented fact, path or API, or a wrong summary after compaction.
terms.origin: General language-model field; one of my seven metrics.

terms.definition: Throughput, efficiency, token count, token cost, time taken, quality of output and hallucinations: what I judge every bottleneck and idea by. Part 2 defines each.
terms.origin: My correction of 14 November 2026.

terms.definition: A Claude Code setting that returns output faster on the models that support it.
terms.origin: Claude Code feature.

terms.definition: One call to the model inside a session: it re-reads the whole window, then acts once. The median step in November’s clinic sessions took 6,600 ms [M].
terms.origin: Our token measurement and the timing of 11 November (MSR-50).

terms.definition: In the split rule, a repository file with one row per piece of work: owner, state and where its result is. A fresh inner session can take over from it.
terms.origin: The split rule (WP12).

terms.definition: An agent on a fixed prompt reads a brief or a compaction summary twice and marks each statement of the latest state right or wrong, and each open loop carried or dropped.
terms.origin: The split rule (WP12), part 6.4.
